html:
The imperial mosque built by Mimar Sinan for Suleiman the Magnificent from 1550 to 1557, on one of Istanbul's hills above the Golden Horn. It is the largest mosque of the city's old core and crowns its skyline.

Its great dome, about 53 metres high, rests on four huge piers and two half domes, a plan that answered the domed church of Hagia Sophia nearby. Windows ring the base of the dome and fill the hall with light. Four minarets stand at the corners of the courtyard, often said to mark Suleiman as the fourth sultan to rule from Istanbul.

The mosque is the heart of a large complex built as a charitable trust of the Ottoman Empire: colleges, a medical school, a hospital, a kitchen that fed the poor, a bath and an inn. Suleiman and his wife Hurrem Sultan are buried in tombs in its garden, and Sinan's own small tomb stands just outside the walls. It was damaged by fire in 1660 and by earthquakes and has been restored several times.
sum: The imperial mosque built by Mimar Sinan for Suleiman the Magnificent from 1550 to 1557, on one of Istanbul's hills above the Golden Horn. It is the largest mosque of the city's old core and crowns its skyline.
